raw_response:
For C30, three catalogue-discovered mechanisms are useful for designing buffer-to-string construction. Each came from the opened [Awesome C++ catalogue](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/fffaraz/awesome-cpp/master/README.md), followed by primary-source verification. This is an internal-model translation, not evidence of deployment or demonstrated benefit in Swift.

1. **[utf8proc: explicit length versus NUL termination](https://github.com/JuliaStrings/utf8proc/blob/master/utf8proc.h).** Its optional NUL-termination flag separates termination policy from input length, preserving interior NUL in counted input and reporting errors. Lower-level decomposition and reencoding allow control over destination storage. Transfer caveat: the convenience mapping operation allocates, and optional transformations can change text. The exact verified API date is **unknown**: [release notes](https://github.com/JuliaStrings/utf8proc/blob/master/NEWS.md) establish v1.3.1 on 2015-11-02, but historical-header fetches failed.

2. **[RapidJSON: counted strings with explicit ownership choices](https://rapidjson.org/structrapidjson_1_1_generic_string_ref.html).** Pointer-plus-length references support interior NUL and avoid rescanning or copying when the source lifetime is sufficient; [GenericValue](https://rapidjson.org/classrapidjson_1_1_generic_value.html) also supplies copying constructors. This suggests making known length and storage ownership explicit in the API. Transfer caveat: borrowing requires lifetime guarantees, and a string reference alone does not validate Unicode. Availability of this precise API by the cutoff is **unknown**. The [changelog](https://rapidjson.org/md__c_h_a_n_g_e_l_o_g.html) separately dates counted Document::Parse overloads to 2016-08-25, after the cutoff.

3. **[simdutf: validating bulk transcoding](https://github.com/simdutf/simdutf).** Its validating conversions consume a pointer plus a byte or code-unit count and write into caller storage, providing a later implementation reference for efficient bounded conversion. Transfer caveat: destination capacity and Swift ownership still require design, and variants that assume valid input must not be substituted for validation. This is **post-decision evidence**: the project's own citation identifies 2021, later than 2016-02-23.

The translation suggested by these mechanisms is to expose input bounds, encoding, malformed-input behavior, and ownership explicitly. A caller using a different delimiter can supply the selected buffer range; validation still has to account for incomplete code units at that boundary. This synthesis is a design inference, not a verified implementation result.

The search stopped at the conservative 25-open-attempt limit, counting repeated and failed attempts. ICU and libiconv primary pages repeatedly failed, GLib's primary repository failed, and historical API retrieval was incomplete. Those failures were recorded rather than filled in from memory. Two catalogue-restricted queries produced these three retained candidates; no excluded proposal was recognized in the retrieved material.

ICU and GNU libiconv primary pages each failed twice; the GLib repository returned HTTP 406. These projects were not retained as verified candidates.

Two utf8proc historical header attempts and one RapidJSON historical tutorial attempt returned DisabledError. Existing older releases do not establish the age of the exact live API, so two candidate dates remain unknown.
simdutf is later evidence, with a project citation year of 2021. No performance benchmark was run or independently validated.
No excluded target proposal was recognized in search snippets or opened pages. Model pretraining knowledge cannot be erased; memory leakage is not controlled.
Translation was performed by the internal model in a separate context, not by human participants. C/C++ APIs require adaptation to Swift lifetime, storage, error-handling, and Unicode semantics.
